what: how each compiler lays out values in JavaScript: hazel-jit on 2026-11-07 and report 046's three others, from report 046's table; hazel-jit now from HazelJit.re on hazel-jit (#2859) at be44756900, with the day's changes merged on 2026-11-25 (loops, JS arguments, constructors made once, a module's members by name, === against a literal)

rows.value: a list cell; the empty list

rows.hazel-jit 2026-11-07: an array, each label also a property

rows.hazel-jit now: a named one: f.$d(a, b), its parts as JS arguments; else one argument, an array
r["x"] behind a check; a module's member, its own variable
i === 0 against a literal; else $R.eq(a, b)
a call of itself: a turn of a for (;;) loop; else a call

suggestions.what: Pass a function's arguments as JS arguments.
suggestions.now: A function bound to a name, whose parameter is a tuple pattern, has a direct form with the parts as its JS parameters; a call with the tuple written out goes to it with no array (43828037c9). A function made where it is passed keeps one argument.
== against a number, string or boolean written out is === (0ce95a2e8f, merged); between two Ints held in variables it is still $R.eq, which is small enough for the engine to inline.

A recursive function's calls of itself in tail position are a for (;;) loop, its variables declared per pass (50b70d5a40). Calls of another function in tail position, and mutual recursion, are still calls, as in ReScript and Melange.

suggestions.what: Unbox options, and make constructors flat.
suggestions.now: Constructors without arguments, None among them, are one constant each (ae29353ff0, merged), so None is no longer made anew; Some(t) is still {$c: "Some", $v: t}, and Take(a, b, k) still holds its arguments in an inner array. Options unboxed were measured from a bench build only (^ticket(858)).

suggestions.what: Lay out labeled tuples as objects only.
suggestions.now: A tuple whose every entry is labeled is a plain object (9ec865976d), and a field read is the property behind a check: 0.63 of the time on the games.
